headline: Afraid of the 'zeal'
summary: A Bible verse from John, chapter 2, about zeal for God's house eating one up frightens Teedie, who imagines the 'zeal' as a beast hiding in churches. He later tells the story in his third Earl Lecture in March 1911, printed in Realizable Ideals (1912). Edith's grandmother, Emily Lee Tyler, dies.

events.detail: Teedie is scared by a verse from the Gospel of John
Emily Lee Tyler, Edith Carow's grandmother, dies

uncertain: Date is approximate for the childhood fear; Earl Lecture reference is a later retelling.

headline: The best man he ever knew
summary: In later life Roosevelt sums up his father as the finest man he knew, strong and brave yet gentle and generous, and intolerant of selfishness, cruelty, idleness, cowardice or lying in his children.

events.detail: Roosevelt's later tribute to his father

tr_quotes.text: My father, Theodore Roosevelt, was the best man I ever knew. he combined strength and courage with gentleness, tenderness, and great unselfishness. He would not tolerate in us children selfishness or cruelty, idleness, cowardice, or untruthfulness.

uncertain: Recollection placed on this date by the compiler.

headline: Summer at Loantaka
summary: The Roosevelts spend the summer at Loantaka in New Jersey. Roosevelt later remembered how the children adored the country, disliked the city, and hated the autumn move back to town.

events.detail: Family summers at Loantaka, New Jersey

tr_quotes.text: We children, of course, loved the country beyond anything. We disliked the city. We were always wildly eager to get to the country when Spring came, and very sad when in the late Fall the family moved back to town.
